g.text: We kept each region’s usual spawning months and asked: does heat reach them more often now? In 10 of 14 regions, yes.
In Northern Taiwan and the Gulf of Aqaba it hits about a quarter of a typical recent season. Four regions stay clear.
Heat now reaches the spawning months, unevenly
Heat here means 4 or more NOAA degree heating weeks, the level where corals are likely to bleach. Months are weighted by recorded spawning. The right column compares 2015–24 with 1986–95.
This shows overlap only: it cannot show that spawning moved or failed. Sources: Baird et al. (2021), NOAA Coral Reef Watch.
